title: Patch: the AI prices Evasive units for what the keyword protects

**Issue #4761 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4761: Patch: the AI prices Evasive units for what the keyword protects
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Evasive means no attack can target the unit, not even a forced one, and no Spell or Field Spell can target it either, not even its owner's. The AI already plays legally around all of that, because the engine simply never offers it those moves. But when it weighs a board, an Evasive unit counts exactly like an ordinary unit with the same stats: nothing for the keyword. So it will swap its own Evasive attacker into an even trade it should refuse, undervalue Evasive cards when it picks its opening hand, and price enemy Evasive threats as if removal it cannot cast could still reach them. A concrete table: the AI holds Jlockeed's J15 Fighter, a Ranged, Flying, Rush, Evasive unit, and trades it even-up for a vanilla body of the same size, where the protection alone should have kept it swinging past removal. Practice players and ladder-bot opponents notice.

## Why

- SPEC §6 made Evasive protection strictly stronger than Immune to Spells against attacks, with the same spell-untargetability including its owner's spells, minus Defense Position (R3543002, R3551003, R4353002).
- `KeywordWeights` in `crates/ai/src/config.rs` names every older combat keyword down to Windfury and has no Evasive arm, so `of()` answers `None`; the keyword loops in `unit_worth` and `face_worth` (`crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs`) add 0, and `hand_card_value` (mulligan keeps, R4110000) plus the reply's trade pricing inherit the 0.
- The only mention of Evasive in `crates/ai` is the retired learn lane's uncounted-keyword list in `features.rs` (R4159000): the shipping evaluation never learned it either.
- The footprint is live, not theoretical: printed on C+ #51 Jlockeed's J15 Fighter and S+ #46 Phase Fabric's Radiant face, on the Jade Beauty and Loitering Munition tokens, and granted mid-game by C #32 Felinor Feelings and Stinkyscape #140 Rush Token Launcher. The shadow ban is empty and no set is gated, so AI decks and their opponents hold these cards today.
- Precedent exists for exactly this change: the Pierce weight (R346), the conservative Ranged/Flying starts (#841), and windfury screened to 0.0 (#1602).
- Nothing open or closed already covers it: #4735 is engine prompt legality, and the rejected #4538 (fuzz monitor), #4338 (static splash valuation) and #4514 (secret ruling-out) are all different work.
- Checked and deliberately excluded: the Taunt walk needs no change. Attackers that `attack_restriction` refuses against a Taunt (Evasive included, `crates/engine/src/restrictions.rs`) fall into the walk's unbound half in `soak_past_taunts`, so an Evasive Taunt already binds nobody per R3551003. Verified by reading the walk; no behavior change proposed there.

## Proposal

1. Add an `evasive` entry (serde `Evasive`) to `KeywordWeights` plus its `of()` arm. Proposed start 1.0, mirroring `immune_to_spells`: same can't-buff-it downside, stronger attack protection, offset by never defending. The screen sets the value, not judgment. `GREEDY_EVAL` keeps 0.0 so the §9.9 gates measure against an unchanged yardstick.
2. Update the two `KeywordWeights` literals in `crates/ai/tests/ai/evaluate.rs`; add scene tests in that file's style (`unit_worth`/`face_worth` diff equals the weight) plus one behavioral test (the AI keeps its Evasive attacker over an even vanilla trade) that fails without the weight.
3. Screen per `training/improve.md`, A screen. Fork screen with `--save` preferred: Evasive acts in a minority of games, which the deal screen buries (R4397000, R4607000). Keep only on `forkEdgeLow` above 0 and record the tally in the knob's config comment; if inconclusive, ship 0.0 with the screen recorded, as windfury did.
4. No ruling note (tuning, not a rules decision), no spec change, no shadow-ban touch (`improve.md` forbids it).

## Where it lands

- `crates/ai/src/config.rs` (`KeywordWeights`, `of()`, `AI_EVAL`, `GREEDY_EVAL`)
- `crates/ai/tests/ai/` (the two literals in `evaluate.rs` plus new Evasive scene tests)
- Cites SPEC §6 Evasive, §9.9 gates, R3543002/R3551003/R4353002/R4110000; process per `training/improve.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `KeywordWeights::of(KeywordKind::Evasive)` returns the new entry and every other kind is unchanged (existing `keyword_weights_of_answers_each_kind_its_own_entry` still green)
- [ ] The new scene tests fail with the entry at 0/removed and pass with it
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-ai`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p jackioh-ai --all-targets -- -D warnings` green
- [ ] Screen tally recorded in the knob's config comment; value kept only on `forkEdgeLow` (or `edgeLow`) above 0
- [ ] Gate yardstick untouched: the `GREEDY_EVAL`/`GREEDY_MULLIGAN` diff is empty

## Size and risks

Small diff, about 20 lines of config plus tests (difficulty hard: AI work). The screen dominates the cost: the `turn_hook`/`activation` fork screens took 3-4 hours on 4 cores, so pass `--save` inside the worktree so a cut run resumes. Risk one: Evasive's downsides (owner's own Spells barred, never defends) could make 1.0 too rich; the screen decides, and an inconclusive screen ships 0.0. Risk two: none to gates or players if reverted; the whole change is one number behind `AI_EVAL`.
```
